domain: wildfire operations - municipal fire-alert onset prediction (Brazil, all biomes; INPE reference-satellite active-fire detections)
prediction_question: A Brazilian municipality has recorded zero active-fire detections (INPE reference-satellite series) for 14 consecutive days through day D. At 13:00 UTC on day D+1 - after INPE's morning consolidation of day-D detections (daily CSV for day D observed published 09:05 BRT on D+1) - given only the municipality's detection history through day D, the calendar, state and biome, will at least one active-fire detection be recorded in that municipality within the next 7 days (event days D+1..D+7)? A useful prediction lets PREVFOGO/IBAMA, state civil defence and municipal fire brigades pre-position crews in a country where detection precedes enforcement, and persistence cannot win by construction.
prediction_time: Instant: 13:00 UTC on day D+1. Features are everything published by then with event time <= D: the complete detection archive through day D (daily file for D observed complete at 09:05 BRT on D+1; detections stream near-real-time at 10-minute granularity during day D), calendar, state/biome. Optional covariates also available at the instant: observed fire-risk grid for day D (NetCDF published ~03:32 server time on D+1) and INPE's forecast risk grids for D+1..D+3 (published on day D). Excluded as post-instant: every detection row with event time > D, and any current-year statistic that only becomes final later. As-of policy: each detection row carries its event timestamp (data_pas / data_hora_gmt); the archive is treated as an append-mostly observation log; LIMITATION (recorded): INPE regenerates archive files (2003-2017 files regenerated 2025-09-08; 2024 file regenerated 2025-06-06) and no historical file vintages are kept, so features are taken from the current archive under the policy that detection rows are immutable observations; construction pins file checksums and must re-fetch one fixed month after >=2 weeks to measure late-row churn before quoting any number.
target_definition: Binary. Positive: >=1 reference-satellite detection with event timestamp in [D+1 00:00, D+8 00:00) located in municipality m; negative: zero such detections. Label source: the same detection rows (data_pas timestamp + municipio/estado name) that feed the feature history - construction derives the label from event-time windows and must not ship any row with event time > D in feature columns (the label column is a derived aggregate, never a carried source column). Population: all Brazilian municipalities (5570 IBGE codes; ref-era files key by name - construction maps names to IBGE codes and asserts the mapping is total over the detection rows). Conditioning: evaluated pairs are municipality-days with zero detections in [D-13, D] (onset-conditioned; raw-pair variant recorded for comparison).

split_strategy: Windows by fire year (July-June or calendar year - construction fixes one definition and records it), temporal, non-overlapping: train 2003-2019, eval 2020-2022, holdout 2023-2025, each window carrying full seasonal cycles. Every measured year holds both classes at large margin: municipality-days with >=1 detection 2019: 53,369; 2020: 54,956; 2022: 49,559; 2024: 62,450 (positives cluster in the dry season and in drought years - reported as clustered counts; onset-conditioned pairs measured on 2024: 1,173,526 evaluated pairs, 88,888 positives = 7.57% base rate; raw pairs 1,535,182 with 244,175 positives = 15.9%). Exact per-window pair counts are computed on the full files at construction (all 23 ref years measured feasible: 4 years = 35.5 MB in 16.9 s on the coordinator). Reference-satellite era consistency: the publisher curates the reference series for comparability and the Estatisticas product uses the same series (cross-check exact), but construction must record the per-era reference satellite from INPE documentation and pin window boundaries on any era change observed in the yearly counts.

measurements.probe_evidence_2026_10_23: Probes (scripts in .factory scratch, summarized in notes.md): dataserver repository listing; annual ref zip inventory 2003-2025 with sizes; 4 ref years fully downloaded and counted; monthly 2024-06 partial schema read (25 MB); daily-file publication lastmods; risk-grid archive ascending listing; Estatisticas CSV cross-check (exact match).
measurements.cost_measured: Discovery: 4 ref-year zips = 35,536,896 B in 16.9 s wall (coordinator container, 4 vCPU); plus ~30 small HTTP listings/page reads. Construction estimate from measured per-file sizes: all 23 ref years ~= 150 MB in one worker job (minutes), plus optional monthly all-satellite files 2024+ (~25-90 MB/month measured/partial) if used.
measurements.publication_lag_measured: Day-D daily CSV complete by 09:05 BRT on D+1 (lastmod pattern measured across 30 daily files); risk grids for D published by ~03:32 on D+1; Estatisticas current-month partial through yesterday (page text). These fix the prediction instant at 13:00 UTC on D+1.
measurements.asof_limitation: No historical vintages of archive files; files regenerated 2025-09-08 (2003-2017) and 2025-06-06 (2024). Detection rows carry event timestamps and are treated as immutable observations; construction measures late-row churn (re-fetch one fixed month after >=2 weeks, compare checksums/row counts) before any number is quoted.

findings: Target window [D+1 00:00, D+8 00:00) begins 13 hours before the 13:00 UTC D+1 prediction instant; label information precedes prediction.

INPE FAQ Q39: Base 2 launched 14 Jun 2018, replaced Collection 5 with 6, reprocessed Terra history since 01 Nov 2000 and Aqua since 04 Jul 2002, corrected 2017 MODIS/VIIRS detections, moved to IBGE 2016 boundaries. Historical rows are retrospectively reprocessed, not operational snapshots.
Current regenerated files and a prospective two-week churn check do not establish historical as-of availability; Last-Modified is not completeness or time zone.

novelty_check.theirs: INPE publishes the detections themselves (free, open, since 1998) plus a daily meteorological fire-DANGER rating (a covariate, not a detection benchmark); no shipped detection-prediction task with splits exists. Closest artifacts: Cerrado ConvLSTM (REIC 24(1) 2026) - 5km Cerrado-only grid, next-day, 2 prototype years, data via Google Drive; arXiv 2606.04170 - Cerrado-Minas Gerais conservation units only, explicitly RETROSPECTIVE ('same-day covariates... rather than a prospective forecast'), rule-bound pseudo-absences, GEE-dependent covariates, public repo without a shipped task artifact; Zenodo 21269005 - detection rows joined to weather (no task, no splits); Kaggle municipal panel - annual covariates only. US wildfire datasets (TS-SatFire, HF wildfire-ignition) are imagery-based, different population/instant
novelty_check.ours: A prospective, instant-honest national benchmark: predict, per Brazilian municipality conditioned on 14 fire-free days, whether >=1 INPE reference-satellite active-fire detection occurs in the next 7 days, from trailing detection history + calendar + biome only (all features published by 09:05 BRT on D+1); exhaustive true-population negatives (no pseudo-absence sampling), year-disjoint train/eval/holdout 2003-2025, publisher danger-rating (FireRiskModel) shipped as a baseline, runner-compatible versioned artifact
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
